Discovering Language Model Behaviors with Model-Written Evaluations

paper.arxiv.2212.09251

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2212.09251v1. Model-generated balanced evaluation examples and instruction/diversity limits establish synthetic evaluation construction. The95.7/95.5 source discrepancy is retained, not harmonized by admission. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Generator/discriminator biases and filtering can narrow diversity, models struggle with unfamiliar concepts or many constraints, and prompt wording or misunderstood instructions can change what an evaluation actually tests.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The method samples evaluation inputs conditional on intended labels and ranks/filters them with a discriminator; persona evaluation used a helpful RLHF generator and its preference model to form label-balanced agree/disagree datasets of at most 1, 000 statements per behavior.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Surge AI workers checked generated inputs and labels; three workers judged each example for 11 full datasets and 100 examples in each of 122 additional datasets, assessing relevance, label correctness and ambiguity.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

In §3.3, the paper reports mean relevance 4.4 ±0.9 on a 1–5 scale, Fleiss κ0.875 between three workers and majority agreement with 95.5% of generated labels; these are validation judgments, not certified correctness of every released example.
